questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement.**

The little girl __fall off from__ the terrace.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 1) i.e. A.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase "fall off from" is grammatically wrong.
 
• The correct choice is **option 1**.
 
• Let's understand the phrasal verb given below:
 
 
• ***​​Fall from- to suddenly go down onto the ground or towards the ground without intending to or by accident.***
 
 
• Example:* He** fell from the terrace** and died.*
 
 
 
 
 
• Hence of the given options,** 'fell from'** is the most appropriate choice.

 

Correct Sentence__:* "The little girl __**fell from**__ the terrace."*

* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__***

 
• *​​Fall off: *If the amount, rate, or quality of something falls off, it becomes smaller or lower:

 
 
• Example: *Sales have been falling off recently.*

questions.question:
**Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error.**

No sooner did I reach the station when the train left.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3) i.e. C.

 *__Explanation__:

__
 
• *Some conjunctions such as: 'No sooner...than', 'Hardly/scarcely...when', are used in a pair.*
 
• For example :
 
 
• Hardly had I left the cinema hall than I saw the actor himself. [IMAGE: https://lh6.googleusercontent.com/Aa6GONxZLq5N02zi2OIojzfQUTFcvlgkVYESn43vAlypHD17p-l0V9arCGHbQaeUJqHEJsMPy7EDzb9cAHybgFmXfY6e700B8DXG29csKDathkAL_LlGhH3TWBcyCpzPAm-pb1i4] 
 
• Hardly had I left the cinema hall when I saw the actor himself. [IMAGE: https://lh5.googleusercontent.com/1RlEYF5CsTxopRygVucClzcLnM_HZTVVPM0OWDB65EC34Ci_IFVRzeWud8LxfKBcgYhONqug9EUxQgWmBqG2qg1u4PTDWQAQXt1x1HpshjbYSRixRVmfnJTaIegewgrAFtoKrbmT] ​​
 
 
 
• Hence in the 3rd part of the sentence, 'than' will be used instead of 'when'.

 [IMAGE: https://lh5.googleusercontent.com/LWUGk5afvUuQ8LUUZ4VCkXpYJrVqRvWMh8zH474fdDy3U6-jfSxEb4p9ZEpNCM99N_B01wXdRtkNu4xJhysCYc06TvjVeMwWPX0YtXBmxRRRIc-gxhQpsexuaGdK8bwbUXRZVfZK] 

 
• *Whenever 'did' is used as an auxiliary/helping verb,** the main verb will be in 1st form.*
 
• In case of these conjunctions, an inverted form of the verb will be used as illustrated in the examples above.*

​

Correct Sentence__:* "**No sooner** did I reach the station** than **the train left."*

questions.question:
Directions: In this section, each of the following sentences has a blank space and each sentence is followed by four options. Select the most appropriate option to fill the blank space.

Anand Kumar is ____ unique teacher.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 4) i.e. D.

 [IMAGE: https://lh4.googleusercontent.com/nH9SOO-Lesl0Tr3WrWxbTZKq5Fi3sMMAFMObqpmj9e8rHx9jeycNJcLsvyjWFjfI914rJX1wg1V5uIIYc-_oEjMgSKxXpCwjdzEWcEhd8AudKOf8F9ps9hvb4TyL2qwPstf5jcBp] __Explanation__: 

 
• ***There are two types of articles:***

 
 
• ***Definite- The.***
 
• ***Indefinite- A, an.***
 
 
 
• In English grammar, we use the indefinite article '**a'** before a singular noun when the specific identity of the noun is not known to the listener or reader, or when it's not important to identify the specific instance of the noun.
 
• Here, 'a unique teacher' doesn't identify a specific teacher; instead, it describes the kind of teacher Anand Kumar is.
 
• ***​Article 'a' is used with consonants whereas 'an' is used with vowels. ***
 
 
• ***If a word starts with a vowel but has a sound of a consonant, 'a' will be used before that word.***
 
 
 
• ​For example:
 
 
• ​Harsh got himself enrolled in** an university****.** [IMAGE: https://lh6.googleusercontent.com/Aa6GONxZLq5N02zi2OIojzfQUTFcvlgkVYESn43vAlypHD17p-l0V9arCGHbQaeUJqHEJsMPy7EDzb9cAHybgFmXfY6e700B8DXG29csKDathkAL_LlGhH3TWBcyCpzPAm-pb1i4] 
 
• Harsh got himself enrolled in** a university*.**** [IMAGE: https://lh5.googleusercontent.com/1RlEYF5CsTxopRygVucClzcLnM_HZTVVPM0OWDB65EC34Ci_IFVRzeWud8LxfKBcgYhONqug9EUxQgWmBqG2qg1u4PTDWQAQXt1x1HpshjbYSRixRVmfnJTaIegewgrAFtoKrbmT] *
 
• ***Here the word 'university' starts with a vowel but has the sound of a consonant and hence will be preceded by 'a'.***
 
 
 
• Hence the most appropriate of the given options is 'a' i.e 4th option.
